dependency_asset_review: Installed 32 distributions from mdanalysis-rmsd-setup (MDAnalysis 2.11.0, MDAnalysisTests 2.11.0, pandas 3.1.0, matplotlib 3.11.2, numpy 2.5.4, scipy 1.18.1 and transitive libs; catalog: 7945 installed files inspected, 3265 candidates). Audited scientific answer exposure by extracting every exported RMSD value from the three CSV artifacts and regex-scanning all installed Python sources for numeric constants matching to within the constant's printed precision. One genuine answer asset found: MDAnalysis/tests (MDAnalysisTests) analysis/test_rms.py, whose fixtures encode expected RMSD values for the exact same AdK PSF/DCD inputs—'correct_values' 4.68953 (line 179) = mass_weighted_rmsd.csv frame 49 C-alpha RMSD 4.689532149658401, and 'single_frame' 0.91544906 (line 249) = the frame-5 mass-weighted C-alpha RMSD 0.9154490678430646. Declared it in dependency-exclusions.json as an unused packaged test module (verified the analysis only imports MDAnalysisTests.datafiles and MSF/DCD/CRD data, not test_rms.py; removal import-checked). All other apparent matches were coincidental: matplotlib colormap stops and trigonometric constants (e.g. 0.82772, 0.90142, 0.87485), MSD/scalar constants at different exponents (4.99977747e-01 vs 4.999), and frame/time integers; frame-0/49 'Backbone/CORE/LID/NMP' groupselection RMSD values in test_rms.py (4.7857, 4.7048, 4.6924 etc.) do not appear in any exported artifact since the notebook's exported tables use C-alpha selections and different group selections. MDAnalysisTests data files (adk.psf, adk_dims.dcd, adk_open.crd) are required imports, not exclusions. Second (final) reference test ran with the exclusion applied: files_removed 1, excluded_files_absent true, exit 0, identical artifact sha256s. Remaining uncertainty: the scan is content-based over decimal constants, not a semantic/exhaustive audit of every package.
explanation: Both reference tests passed (exit 0, all three artifacts produced with stable sha256s; second ran with the declared exclusion applied). Environment: python:3.13.13-slim-bookworm with uv-managed deps MDAnalysis 2.11.0, MDAnalysisTests 2.11.0, pandas 3.1.0, matplotlib 3.11.2 (matplotlib needed to satisfy retained pandas .plot calls; offline no-display rendering verified via headless Agg backend). No system packages, no staged inputs, and an empty staging recipe suffice because all molecular data (adk.psf/adk_dims.dcd/adk_open.crd) travels in the imported MDAnalysisTests distribution; the analysis script is byte-identical to the converted source (sha256 afca4564...). Runtime was ~4.7s within a 600s reference limit. Observed outputs: core_ca_rmsd.csv (98 frames, columns Frame, Time (ns), CORE; frame 49 = 1.652 Å), mass_weighted_rmsd.csv (Frame, Time (ns), C-alphas, CORE, LID, NMP; frame 49 C-alphas = 4.68953 Å), resid_weighted_rmsd.csv (same columns; frame 97 NMP = 13.912 Å). Dependency audit found one bundled answer asset—MDAnalysisTests/analysis/test_rms.py—which embeds reference RMSD constants for the same AdK trajectory, including 0.91544906 (frame 5 C-alpha RMSD) and 4.68953 (frame 49 C-alpha RMSD, matching mass_weighted_rmsd.csv); it is packaged pytest code never imported by the analysis (verified by temporally removing it and re-importing MDAnalysisTests.datafiles), so it was declared as an exclusion and the final successful reference test was run with it removed.
unresolved_assumptions: MDAnalysis 2.11.0 was selected as a current release supporting the results API (R.results.rmsd) used by the notebook baseline; the notebook was last documented against 2.4.0-dev0. Minor numerical drift versus a 2.4.0 run is possible but the computed exports are internally consistent with the installed version's own shipped test constants (4.68953/0.91544906 for the same trajectory).
Predicate plots execute headlessly via the Agg backend (environment setting only); the plotting calls and their data content are preserved unchanged.
The exclusion of MDAnalysisTests/analysis/test_rms.py removes pytest module code only; MDAnalysisTests data files needed for scientific input remain installed.
The bundled answer-asset scan was precision-based over decimal constants across installed Python sources; conclusions are limited to the content actually inspected.
